disagreement.point: X "young or youthfully adorned" vs Y "young, youthful, and fond of adornments"; source "daharo vā yuvā vā maṇḍanakajātiko"

choice_note: X keeps the formal sutta period and 'outcaste' with Pali flagged in notes; Y uses colloquial short sentences ('saying sorry') and interprets caṇḍāla as 'corpse-worker tribe', cetasā as 'heart'.

disagreement.point: X "exacts the forfeit of drinking" vs Y "descends to drink"; source "下而飲" (commentary: the loser ascends and drinks)

choice_note: X expands the classic text interpretively ('student of virtue', 'Chun-tsze' kept) while Y renders it tersely ('superior man', 'bows and yields') and stays close to the commentary's ritual vocabulary.

disagreement.point: X "The body's strength increases and it becomes free" vs Y "The Satwa of his body becomes free"; source "भवेत्सत्त्वं च देहस्य" (ṭīkā: सत्त्वं बलं)

choice_note: X translates sattva as 'strength' following the commentary and glosses every term; Y leaves 'Satwa' untranslated and folds commentary detail (protruded tongue, Sitkari) silently into the verse; gulma 'abdominal tumors' vs 'colic'.

disagreement.point: X "he showed the same respect as at first" vs Y "even after a long time, he still respected them"; source "久而敬之"

choice_note: X paraphrases expansively ('knew well how to maintain friendly intercourse') in old romanisation; Y gives a plain close rendering in pinyin with bracketed supplements for the commentary.

disagreement.point: X "in reality, there is no coming or going" vs Y "no such condition as 'only one more reincarnation'"; source "而實無往來"

choice_note: X keeps the Sanskrit titles with brief glosses and the sutra's terse paradox; Y expands into Victorian paraphrase with parenthetical definitions ('subject only to one more reincarnation', 'merely a descriptive title').

disagreement.point: X "illusion that the soul is distinct from the Lord" vs Y "erroneous notion of not being distinct from those adjuncts"; source "तद्विवेकभ्रमकृतो"

choice_note: X breaks the bhāṣya into short modern paragraphs with glossed terms ('nerves', 'pericardium' for nāḍī, purītat); Y keeps the dense scholastic objection-reply chain, retains nāḍī/prāṇa/pūrvapakshin and brackets sutra supplements.

disagreement.point: X "attains final knowledge by breaking through in this very life" vs Y "attain enlightenment early on in this very life"; source "diṭṭheva dhamme paṭihacca aññam ārādheti" (v.l. paṭikacca)

choice_note: X keeps formulaic repetition and technical renderings ('final knowledge', 'remainder of clinging', 'final liberation in the interval'); Y uses plain modern idiom ('enlightenment', 'residue left behind', 'extinguished between one life and the next') and fills in abbreviated formulas.

disagreement.point: X "his mind is free from terror or alarm" vs Y "when he is not rash"; source "अनुत्रस्तसंत्रस्तमना"

choice_note: X glosses Sanskrit terms and reads avidhāraṇā avikalpanā as 'non-grasping and non-conceptualizing', paṇḍaka as 'eunuchs', mauṣṭika as 'boxers'; Y keeps terms unglossed with 'law' for dharma, 'refraining from investigating and discussing', 'hermaphrodite', 'jugglers'.
